specification_compliance: Spec line 245 lists known-issues.md as 'four rows removed'; the tree also holds two added rows, with no touch-point revision (SCOPE-3).
_set_pointer at thumbnail_migration.py:49 holds updated_at, which matches spec section 9's 'no ordering change'; no test pins it (R4-TEST-1).
thumbnail_migration.py:93-106 empties the pointers, commits, then unlinks each distinct string, which matches I8 by reading; the two-string removal half has no assertion (R4-TEST-2, TEST-9).
potential_unspecified_behavior: A failed commit on a reused row whose pointer is not yet its slot leaves the newly generated slot file on disk with no pointer naming it (upload.py:363 skips removal). The spec states slot removal only for an upload with a new id. This was read from the code, not exercised, and is not raised as a defect.
regression_risks: Removing updated_at=File.updated_at from _set_pointer would bump updated_at on every migrated row and reorder listings sorted by updated_at, with no test failing (R4-TEST-1).
Changing the reused_row predicate at upload.py:363 to always remove, or to `existing is None`, would not be expected to fail any existing test (TEST-8).
test_coverage: test_two_spellings_of_one_file_count_as_shared asserts pointers and an empty .by-id only, not removal under either name.
No test fails complete_upload's try block over a reused row, or inside the trashed-ghost branch before existing is cleared.

The upload case of test_an_operation_that_fails_before_its_commit_leaves_the_ghost_and_its_picture does not assert the new slot is removed; test_upload_with_a_new_id_whose_commit_fails_leaves_no_slot does assert it for a new id with no existing row.
